did_you_know.text: The title attributes the psalm to David and indicates that it was intended for the director of music—that is, for musical performance as part of worship.

The psalm begins by praising the person who “considers the poor”—someone who pays attention to the vulnerable and offers help. According to the verse, the Lord promises to help such a person in times of trouble.
The blessing for someone who helps the poor includes protection, preservation of life, and defense from enemies. Kindness toward others is thus presented as part of a life under God’s care.
The verse uses the image of a sick person lying on his deathbed and portrays the Lord as caring for him and sustaining him during his illness—a picture of support and comfort in a time of weakness.

The psalmist asks for mercy and healing while acknowledging, “for I have sinned against you.” The request is not only for physical recovery, but also for forgiveness and the restoration of his relationship with the Lord.

The enemies are described as longing for his death and the disappearance of his name. The following verses reveal that they even visit him merely for appearances’ sake, gather harmful rumors about him, and spread them after they leave.
The betrayal is expressed powerfully in the description of “my close friend,” someone who was trusted by the psalmist and even shared his bread, yet ultimately “has lifted his heel against me.”

The closing blessing praises the Lord, the God of Israel, “from everlasting to everlasting,” and ends with “Amen and amen”—a repetition that emphasizes the affirmation of the blessing and its solemn conclusion.
